reden: Yes. The report’s first issue (“Merge credits claimable TITN with no check against TITN balance; late depositors lose TGT”) describes the same root cause and code path as H-1: onTokenTransfer credits claimable without capping it to the TITN deposited (i.e., exceeding TGT_TO_EXCHANGE/TITN_ARB backing), causing later claims to revert and TGT to be stuck. It even ties the numbers (173.7M TITN backing ~579M TGT) and the lack of a deposit cap. The report’s separate issue on withdrawRemainingTitn underflow/brick also matches the second part of H-1, pointing to the same subtraction in withdrawRemainingTitn reverting when totalTitnClaimable exceeds the contract’s TITN balance (including the case caused by oversubscription). The same fix proposed in H-1 (limit total deposits or cap totalTitnClaimable by available TITN) would address the report’s findings for this vulnerability.
